title: Finite exceptional adjunction on normalized coefficient systems over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and choose a compactification $f=pj$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small etale sites put $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$, ordinary compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The ambient etale exceptional adjoint restricts to an exact $A_n$-linear functor $G_n$ on $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$, right adjoint to $F_n:D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)\to D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$. Here $D^b_{ctf}$ consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and Tor amplitude in some finite interval: tensoring with every coefficient-module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology only in that interval [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. The adjunction has the units and counits of the ordinary etale exceptional adjunction.

For $m\geq n$, put $Q_T=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ on $T=X,Y$. Let $q_{m,n}:Q_YF_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nQ_X$ be the canonical compact-support coefficient projection comparison. Its counit transpose is an isomorphism
$$b_{m,n}:Q_XG_m\xrightarrow{\sim}G_nQ_Y,$$
characterized by
$$\epsilon_n\circ F_n(b_{m,n})\circ q_{m,n,G_m}=Q_Y(\epsilon_m).$$
The coefficient comparisons have identity and quotient-cocycle equations, preserve the finite units and counits, and commute with shifts.

For $T=X,Y$ let $\mathscr S_T$ be the abelian category of strict systems of $(A_n)_T$-module sheaves with semilinear maps from level $n+1$ to level $n$, with componentwise exactness [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In $D(\mathscr S_T)$ let $\mathscr N_T$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems $M$ whose every evaluation $M_n$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$. Normalized means that every transition-adjoint $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible; no bound independent of $n$ is imposed. The simultaneous system functor $\mathcal F_f=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ preserves these subcategories and has an exact $R$-linear right adjoint $\mathcal G_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$. There are canonical natural evaluation isomorphisms $e_n\mathcal G_f\cong G_ne_n$. They carry the evaluated system units, counits, and quotient transitions to the finite units, counits, and the coefficient comparisons $b_{m,n}$ above. In particular these are actual adjunction functors and transformations in the derived category of systems, with both triangle identities before evaluation. They are independent of the compactification under the canonical refinement comparisons. No integral inverse limit or integral exceptional adjunction is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, p.57, finite exceptional adjunction and both coefficient squares. The exact coherent adjunction on normalized derived systems is an agent-formulated strengthening of that finite construction, using simultaneous ringed coefficient systems; it is a separate proof obligation, not a verbatim assertion of the paper.
